title: Debug a total that skips a row

screens.prompt: In B8, total every store's sales even though one cell in the column holds text.

hints.syntax: =SUM(B2:B7): the whole block in one reference.
hints.func-sum: Adding the cells one at a time is how a total ends up short. Use SUM over the block.
hints.require-ref: Point at the column, or the range stops where somebody typed a row number by hand.
hints.value: The numbers are 320, 250, 300, 400 and 180, which total 1450. The text in the middle is skipped.
hints.error: #VALUE! means a cell in the range holds text that cannot be added. SUM over the range skips it instead.

reject.why: 570, because the last two stores are outside the range
one text cell in the chain makes the whole total an error
the range starts on row 3, so Brooklyn is missing
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!

screens.prompt: In B7, total January to April without counting the Q1 subtotal row above it.

hints.syntax: =SUM(B2:B5): the four months, stopping above the subtotal.
hints.func-sum: Add the months with SUM rather than by naming the cells one at a time.
hints.require-ref: Read the amount column from the grid so the range covers every month.
hints.value: 320 + 250 + 180 + 140 is 890. Pulling the 750 subtotal in as well gives 1640.
hints.error: A range that starts or ends on the wrong row is not an error in Excel. It is just a wrong number.

reject.why: 1640, because the subtotal row is counted inside the total
140: subtracting the subtotal leaves one month
the right number by hand, which is how the next row gets left out
the range starts on row 3, so January is missing
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the colon is missing, so the range is not a range

docs.explain:
A total that skips a row is nearly always a range problem. The range stops one short, starts one late, or reaches up into a subtotal it should have stayed below. SUM is doing what it was told.

On the first screen one cell in the middle holds text, and SUM steps over it without complaint, so B2:B7 returns 1450. A range drawn by hand around the text stops above the stores further down.

On the second, the row above the answer is a Q1 subtotal of 750, and a range that touches it counts the quarter twice: 890 becomes 1640. Compare the total with a quick manual addition, then select the answer cell and read the highlighted block, which is exactly what the formula sees.

errors.text: A cell in the range holds text that a chain of plus signs cannot add. SUM over the range would have skipped it.
The range names a column or row that no longer exists after rows were deleted.
A range that reaches a subtotal counts the same money twice, and a range that stops early leaves a store out. Neither raises an error.

docs.atWork: A monthly close with a subtotal row above the answer, and an imported list with one unreadable cell.
docs.outcome: Find the row a broken total skips and cover it without double-counting a subtotal.
docs.teaches: SUM over a block with text in it, and stopping a range above a subtotal
docs.dataset: City sales with a gap, and four months plus a subtotal

seo.title: Debug an Excel total that skips a row
seo.description: A total that misses a row is usually a range that stops early or swallows the subtotal above it. Drag the range handles to see what the formula covers.
